summary:
Bullpen_fatigue is the story of this slate stretch, sitting at 70% (16-7, n=23) across every rating model and HOT by a staggering +22.9pts over season baseline for R1-R3 and +23.8pts for R4. Hitting isn't far behind, with R2 and R3 both running 70% (16-7, n=23) and R4 hitting an absurd 78% (18-5, n=23), a +26.2pt jump over its 52% season number. Bullpen itself is riding a 3-win streak across all four ratings, hot at 61% (14-9, n=23) versus a 52% season baseline. On the money side, R3 is the unit leader with a 30-day mark of 50-25 (67%, +33.0u) and a season total of +92.0u — the best raw P/L of the group despite R1 having more season volume. R2's 14-day strong-play window is the hottest short-term read anywhere in the data: 4-1 (80%, +6.0u, n=5).

Today's slate is a single game, and it's a split decision — CLE @ CHW has R1, R3, and R4 all leaning CHW (+0.08, +0.16, +0.05) while R2 is the lone dissenter on CLE (-0.20). With only one game on the board, there's no category-combo cluster to lean on, but the structural signal still matters: three of four ratings agree on CHW, and R3 — the unit-P/L leader at +92.0u season and 67% over the last 30 days — has the strongest same-side delta of the group at +0.16. R2, the one pointing to CLE, is riding its own hot streak (80% strong-play hit rate over 14 days), so this isn't a case of fading a cold outlier — it's the rare split where both sides are backed by live heat. Neither CLE nor CHW shows up in the top team-volume list, so there's no is a historical team trend to lean into here; this one comes down to trusting the majority rating consensus (CHW) while being aware R2's recent form is sharp enough to not dismiss outright. If bullpen_fatigue or hitting ratings are feeding into CHW's lean, that's the signal worth weighting given how extreme those categories are running across the board right now.
